terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A parked vehicle prop: an exterior shell with no interior geometry, since a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside and the glazing is authored as a tinted, mostly opaque pane. The wheels are the mechanisms: each is a named pivot on its axle. Nothing else moves and nothing attaches, so there are no sockets. A single-cab pickup converted to a fixed-route shared taxi. The plate shows a dusty yellow cab and bed, a rusty steel-tube frame over the bed carrying a pale corrugated sheet roof with a rack rim, two brown bench seats along the sides with backs above the bed rails, a rusted bed floor, a rear step and steel wheels.

reasoning: The identity is the side profile -- bonnet, single cab, and an open bed under a tube cage carrying a corrugated roof -- and it is one closed polygon swept across the width, with the wheel arches cut into it as notches, then narrowed above the belt for tumblehome. One geometry carries the whole shell.
One repetition system: four wheels off one lathe, each a named pivot on its axle.
A colour difference is not a material difference: every trim tone -- tyre, rim, bumper, lamp -- is a vertex colour on one white material, and the paint carries its dirt as a canvas.
Action readiness is the wheels: four hinge pivots, convex collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A vehicle cannot be a box on a box: the raked screen, the tumblehome and the arches are what make it read at prop distance, and all three come from shaping one extrusion. The glasshouse is a second extrusion of the cab polygon offset 6 mm proud so no pane shares a plane with the body. The bed carries the conversion: six uprights and three rails a side in rusted steel tube, a corrugated sheet roof with a rack rim, two facing benches with backs, an open rear with a step. The cage is OPEN by construction, so the turntable sees the backdrop through it -- that is the vehicle, not a hole in the model.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: bonnet, single cab, and an open bed under a tube cage carrying a corrugated roof as one side outline with two arch notches
tinted glass band round the cabin with painted pillars standing proud of it
two-bar grille between rectangular lamps over a grey bumper; a steel step and low bumper at the open rear
four dusty pressed-steel wheels with dished rims and vent rings on 0.72 m tyres
tan road dust along the sills, lower doors and bed sides, heaviest behind the wheels
door mirrors, handles, shut lines, steps, indicators
open bed with side walls and rail caps, no tailgate
six rusted tube uprights with three rails a side, cross bars and a rack rim on the roof
two facing timber benches with backs above the bed rails, over a rusted floor
corrugated sheet roof overhanging the cab back

resolvedUnknowns: The front elevation is built to type: a two-bar grille between rectangular lamps over a grey bumper.

The cage is open: the turntable gate's enclosed-background signal fires at all four azimuths on the backdrop seen between the rails, above the cab under the overhanging sheet, and out the open rear. --allow-holes is set on that reading, with the _holecc thickness measurement logged per azimuth; it is not an unexplained failure.
The bed floor, benches and cage are in the plate; the rear step is in the plate; no tailgate.

Third pass (2026-09-02) measured the hero render against the plate region by region: the paint had rendered a desaturated beige #dbc897 (sat 0.31) against the plate door #e0b352 (sat 0.63) and is now #d8a850; the windscreen rendered #d1d1cc (luma 208) against #60584d (89) and carries a sky-gradient tile at roughness 0.42; the frame rendered tan #7b6a5a against the plate #362a1d and is #4e3a28; the wheels were closed grey domes and are a steel lathe with dish, vent ring and hub cap.
No interior to the cab: a solid in paint under a 6 mm proud tinted pane.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 1.80 x 2.25 x 5.40 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=8000 triangles, <=6 draw calls, <=4 materials, <=8 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus one named pivot per wheel (4); zero sockets; convex collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center at tyre contact, +Y up, +Z FORWARD, +X the vehicle's left. Meshy returned the proxy with its long axis on X, an arbitrary output convention; the band comparison detects the mismatch from the two footprints and rotates the reference a quarter turn before measuring.

silhouette.description: Sill 0.45 m, wheels 0.72 m in diameter at z +1.78 and -1.35, bonnet lip 0.88-0.96 m to a scuttle at 1.12 m, windscreen raked from z 1.50 to a 0.12 m roof-corner arc into a cab roof at 1.80 m, a matching rear arc into a vertical cab back at z 0.20 dropping to a bed floor at 0.80 m and rails at 1.12 m; fender/roof shoulder filleted at 0.12 m, nose rounded in plan at 0.22 m; uprights from the rails to 2.15 m, sheet at 2.155-2.185 m over z -2.64..0.20 (overhanging the cab back), rack rim to 2.225 m. Benches 0.42 m wide at 1.05 m with backs to 1.45 m.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -0.90..+0.90 on the shell (mirrors to +-1.02); y 0.00 to 2.225 at the roof rack rim; z -2.70..+2.70, +Z forward. The Meshy proxy normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.495 : 0.444 (2.02 lengths tall against the declared 2.40), so heights are proxy fractions of H and stations fractions of L at the declared metres.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.495 : 0.444, i.e. 5.40 x 2.67 x 2.40 m at the declared length -- taller and wider than the registry by 19 and 33 percent, the proxy reading the plate's high viewpoint as height and its cage as width. Heights are proxy fractions of H: bed roof 1.00, cab roof 0.80, bed rail 0.50, bed floor 0.35, wheel top 0.32, sill 0.20; stations bonnet 0.03-0.27 L, cab 0.30-0.55 L, cage 0.55-0.98 L; axles 0.17 L and 0.75 L. The proxy's roof line is continuous over cab and cage; the plate shows the sheet overhanging the cab back, which is what is built.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.70: the plate is a rear three-quarter from above; grille, lamps and front bumper are built to type and to the proxy's front elevation.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-paint (bed side, PBR confidence 0.771) at #bf9c66, the plate door at #e0b352 (sat 0.63) and the cab roof at #d7ba81; the second build shipped #c9a86c and rendered a desaturated beige, so the clean yellow is authored #d8a850. The lower dust #b2925f is darker than the yellow in R and G but BRIGHTER in B, so a plain multiplier clamped and the wash vanished: the material carries E = the per-channel max #d8a85f and a 512 px mud tile paints the yellow as ratio(#d8a850, E) and the dust as ratio(#b2925f, E), both in linear space -- solid to 0.18 of a 2.6 m height-keyed tile, out at 0.40, spray zoned behind the front wheel, along the bed side and ahead of the rear arch, upward faces keyed clean.
Textureless as DECLARED: the dust is a 512 px Canvas 2D mud tile bound after construction as map.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 6,262/8,000 triangles, 5/6 draw calls, 4/4 materials, 5/8 unique geometries, three canvases at 2.0 MB, factory ~70 ms. Turntable: enclosed background is the open cage, allowed on measurement. Colliders re-derived: 8 boxes, coverage 0.958.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: 4 components and one repetition system: 5 of 6. The pillars ride the shell; every trim part rides one merge.

materials.note: paint, glass and a white vertex-coloured trim plus the corrugated sheet: 4 of 4. Tyres, rims, bumpers and lamps differ in albedo only.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 6,262 of 8,000: one extrusion with two 8-segment arches, a 20-segment wheel lathe, and boxes.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A closed side-profile polygon extruded across the width and shaped per vertex (tumblehome above the belt, plan rounding at nose and tail); an offset extrusion of the cabin polygon for the glass; a lathe for the wheel; boxes for everything else.
One InstancedMesh carries the four wheels; the right-side instances are yawed a half turn so the dish faces out. No per-instance colour, so the white base is inert.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. THREE Canvas 2D tiles are bound after construction: a 512 px zoned mud tile on the paint, a 256 px corrugation tile on the sheet as map and bumpMap, and a 256 px sky-gradient glass tile on the glazing. 2.0 MB of texture VRAM, factory ~70 ms.

risks.description: The turntable gate's enclosed-background signal fires on the open cage at every azimuth.
risks.mitigation: That background is real open air: between the rails, above the cab under the overhang, out the rear. --allow-holes set on the _holecc measurement per azimuth, logged in the gate run.

risks.description: The proxy is 19 percent taller than the registry.
risks.mitigation: Declared metres win; heights are proxy fractions; reported as the declared aspect.

risks.description: Grille and lamps built to type.
